To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Borexino detector has been shown to be capable of measuring the 7 Be solar neutrino flux with an accuracy of 7% and the pep neutrino flux with a precision of 20%.

(i) the Borexino Phase I data are consistent with a solar origin of the neutrinos, (ii) the 7Be neutrino flux is measured with 10% accuracy, (iii) the 7 Be solar neutrino interaction rate is consistent with a standard oscillation hypothesis with a mixing angle of 34.4° and no matter effects.
the 7 Be solar neutrinos are detected with an interaction rate of (46.0±3.0)SNU, the pep neutrinos are detected at a rate of (1.06±0.20)SNU, and the CNO neutrinos are not observed.

the study of solar neutrinos in the energy range 0.5 - 2.2 MeV.
the study of low energy solar neutrinos and their interaction with matter.

Borexino has achieved its primary goal of measuring the flux of the low energy solar neutrinos with a level of precision that is unprecedented in the field of solar neutrino research.
, after three years of operation, Borexino has achieved its primary goal of detecting and measuring solar neutrinos in the energy region between 250 keV and 2.6 MeV.

Borexino is the first experiment to measure the solar neutrino flux in the energy range between 0.6 MeV (the threshold for the 7 Be solar neutrino detection) and 1.3 MeV (the energy of the CNO neutrinos).
